facts.text: The README states that the launch file starts a Gazebo simulation in pause with a single robot, runs the panda_control_AIC node by default, and the operator presses play.
The README's installation asks for ros-kinetic-desktop-full.
The README sources /opt/ros/kinetic/setup.bash inside the container image.
The README's troubleshooting says that with ROS Melodic and Gazebo 9 the robot meshes will probably not be shown and tells the user to remove the transparent attribute in the visual .dae files.
simulation.launch declares the paused argument with default true and passes it to the gazebo_ros empty_world launch.
simulation.launch declares use_sim_time with default true and passes it to the gazebo_ros empty_world launch.
simulation.launch loads the robot description under /robot1 and spawns the joint_state_controller plus one effort controller for each of the seven panda joints.
simulation.launch starts the panda_control_AIC node without a namespace and leaves the MRAC node commented out.
panda_control.yaml configures joint_state_controller as joint_state_controller/JointStateController with publish_rate 1000.
panda_control.yaml configures panda_joint1 through panda_joint7 each as an effort_controllers/JointEffortController on that joint.
panda_arm_world.urdf.xacro instantiates panda_arm and the gazebo and transmission macros, and the hand instantiation is commented out.
The panda_arm macro declares ${arm_id}_joint8 as revolute with effort 1, lower 0 and upper 0.1.
The panda transmission macro loads the gazebo_ros_control plugin from libgazebo_ros_control.so.
The panda transmission macro declares hardware_interface/EffortJointInterface transmissions for joint1 through joint8.

The AIC constructor creates seven absolute std_msgs/Float64 publishers named /robot1/panda_joint1..7_controller/command, subscribes to /robot1/joint_states, and also creates publishers for panda_free_energy and the controller's belief and sensory-error topics; it creates no service server.
The AIC constructor subscribes to the absolute /robot1/joint_states and passes AIC::jointStatesCallback as its handler.
AIC.h includes sensor_msgs/JointState.h, which declares the type used by the joint-state subscription.
AIC::jointStatesCallback copies position[i] and velocity[i] for i from 0 to 6 without reading the joint names.
AIC::computeActions computes one torque per joint and publishes the seven values through tauPub1 to tauPub7.
AIC::computeActions updates the torque vector u from its previous value by a gradient step on the position and velocity errors.
AIC::minimiseF calls computeActions, then publishes the free-energy scalar through IFE_pub and the sensory prediction error and belief arrays.

The AIC main loop runs at ros::Rate(1000), calls minimiseF while the node is alive, and cycles between hardcoded desired joint positions every 6000 cycles; it has no service, action, cancellation or reset path.
The AIC desired joint positions are hardcoded in main and are not read from a parameter, topic or service.
The Panda arm xacro states effort 87 on the joint1, joint2, joint3 and joint4 limit lines and effort 12 on the joint5, joint6 and joint7 limit lines.
The gazebo_ros gzserver wrapper adds libgazebo_ros_api_plugin to the server's plugins unless the arguments already name it.
empty_world.launch starts the Gazebo server as the node named gazebo of package gazebo_ros, with the physics engine argument -e $(arg physics).
empty_world.launch defaults its physics argument to ode.
empty_world.launch defaults its gui argument to true.
When gui is true, empty_world.launch starts the node gazebo_gui of type gzclient.
empty_world.launch passes -u to the server when its paused argument is true.
The API plugin calls ros::init with the node name gazebo when ROS is not initialised yet.
The API plugin creates its node handle in the private namespace ~ and advertises its topics and services there.
The API plugin advertises the service pause_physics with the std_srvs::Empty type on its own callback queue gazebo_queue_.
The API plugin advertises the service get_physics_properties with the gazebo_msgs::GetPhysicsProperties type on gazebo_queue_.
gazeboQueueThread serves gazebo_queue_ in a loop with a 0.001 s wall-clock wait while the node handle is ok.
pausePhysics calls world_->SetPaused(true) and returns true.
unpausePhysics calls world_->SetPaused(false) and returns true.
getPhysicsProperties sets res.pause to world_->IsPaused().
getPhysicsProperties sets success true only when the physics engine type is ode; for any other engine it sets success false and returns false.
The GetPhysicsProperties response field pause is true if the physics engine is paused.
Among the world-update begin hooks that its comment says apply forces and publish sim time on /clock, the API plugin connects publishSimTime.
gazebo_ros_control connects its Update to the world-update begin event.
gazebo_ros_control's Update reads the simulation time, updates the controllers and writes their commands to the simulated joints.
World::Step advances simulation time and calls Update only when the world is not paused, a step increment is pending or a reset is due; otherwise it adds the step to the pause time.
World::Step holds worldUpdateMutex while it steps the world.
World::SetPaused stores the paused flag under worldUpdateMutex.
World::IsPaused returns the stored paused flag.
World::Update fires the worldUpdateBegin event and then updates every model.
World::Step calls ProcessMessages after the paused or unpaused branch, so pending messages are processed on every step, paused or not.
A WorldControl message with step calls OnStep, and one with multi_step pauses the world and sets the number of steps to run while paused.

determinism.notes: Event-driven recording fake with no physics step or pacing; placeholder joint samples do not establish trajectory, torque or state-hash replay

gaps: the fake is a ROS-free recording transport: it answers the declared joint-state and free-energy subscriptions, records the declared effort publications and answers the two companion Gazebo services; it runs no Gazebo, physics step, controller manager, AIC loop or MoveIt
the joint positions, velocities, efforts and free energy are placeholders; a live run must receive them from the operator's Gazebo and panda_control nodes

the AIC publishes torques at ros::Rate(1000) (AIC_controller.cpp:62; the torque update is AIC.cpp:154 and the publishes are AIC.cpp:157-162) and will overwrite a single driver publication on the next cycle; the fake records the publication but does not model that race or any motion

the stop is the companion gazebo_ros world pause: the fake keeps a paused flag that /gazebo/pause_physics sets and /gazebo/get_physics_properties reports; it runs no Gazebo World::Step, and its GetPhysicsProperties numbers are placeholders

no unpause is offered: stopping panda_control_AIC does not clear retained joint_effort_command_ (default_robot_hw_sim.cpp:315-316 applies the last command on the next update unless e_stop_active_) or the AIC torque state u (AIC.cpp:43 is an empty destructor and AIC_controller.cpp:93 returns without clearing it; AIC.cpp:154 updates u from its previous value and AIC.cpp:157-162 publishes it). The world stays paused until an operator-reviewed procedure has independently verified that those retained controller commands are cleared or reinitialized. This package does not provide that procedure

while paused, with no step pending and no reset due, /robot1/joint_states (published by joint_state_controller from gazebo_ros_control's world update) and /clock are silent: the joint-state read fails NOT_READY after its 2 s timeout (the fake silences it while its flag is set); the device resource reads no topic, and each effort receipt reports the value it sent

the AIC loop is paced by ros::Rate(1000) at AIC_controller.cpp:62 under use_sim_time true; whether it keeps publishing while /clock is silent is roscpp behaviour outside the clone and the companions, so the fake keeps answering /panda_free_energy while paused and a live free-energy read while paused is unverified. A confirmed pause writes no effort unless a step is pending or a reset is due

a live world can be unpaused or stepped by the Gazebo GUI that empty_world.launch opens by default, by a WorldControl message or by any ROS client; safety_status returns the cached confirmation and does not call get_physics_properties again, so it cannot detect an external unpause or step
the read-back needs the ODE engine (empty_world.launch's default physics): with another engine get_physics_properties returns false and the e-stop stays unconfirmed with the latch held

the deployment's gazebo_ros and Gazebo must be the pinned 2.5.21 (Kinetic) and 7.16.1 releases the companion citations name; the README also mentions ROS Melodic with Gazebo 9 (README.md:73), a deployment this package does not serve; rosbridge cannot read their versions
the launch starts Gazebo paused (the README says to press play), so a live joint-state sample may not arrive until the world runs; the e-stop's read-back already reads pause true then
camera, depth, TF, collision detection, MoveIt planning, the box publisher and the web UI are outside this package
the effort envelope is operator_required: the xacro effort attribute is unsigned and no signed command bound is stated; site-limits.example.json is an example overlay only

safe_state.description: The Gazebo world is paused and the read-back reported pause true. World::Step still updates when a step is pending or a reset is due; otherwise gazebo_ros_control writes no effort. The flag is not a measured standstill. No unpause is offered. Stopping panda_control_AIC does not clear retained joint effort or the AIC torque state u. The world stays paused until an operator-reviewed procedure has independently verified that those retained controller commands are cleared or reinitialized.
